text:
aj-m: FYI — ran into a blocking issue while trying to reserve ND40rs in australiaeast; looks like the quota is tied to the old subscription and we can’t attach reservation to the new one. :grimacing:
maria: Ugh, is this the subscription swap we did last week? which subscription ID is it bound to?
tomas: It’s bound to sub-0a1b2c. New subscription is sub-9f8e7d. Azure portal shows the quota in the old sub and reservation SKU only available in that billing scope.
aj-m: Correct. I tried creating an escalation but the normal quota request flow errors with: "Quota cannot be increased because subscription has active reservations on other scope".
chen: Can we move the reservation scope or transfer resource ownership? My read: reservations are per billing account and require support to reassign.
maria: If support can’t reassign, fallback plan is to spin up on westeurope or southeastasia where ND40rs is available and then migrate workloads. Cost + latency tradeoffs though.
aj-m: I opened a support request: SR#2026-08942. Included subscription mapping, reservation ids, and the exact error screenshot. Azure-support replied asking for billing account owner confirmation.
azure-support: Thanks for the details — we can either (1) re-scope the reservation to the new subscription's billing account pending approval, or (2) create a capacity reservation in the same region on the new subscription and migrate. Please provide billing owner email.
maria: Billing owner is finance+cloud@redwood.com — I’ll loop them in.
tomas: Recorded the follow-ups in the ticket. Also flagged potential network limit issue: new subscription has default vnet/subnet port limits that will block our pod density on ND nodes. Need NSG and subnet port increases.
chen: Good catch. For subnet port limits we need to request 'VM NICs per Subnet' and 'SNAT ports' increase. I’ll draft a support form.
aj-m: Posting the CLI snippet I used to validate quotas — feel free to reuse:
```
az vm list-usage --location australiaeast --query "[?name.value=='Standard_ND40rs_v2'].{Name:name.value, CurrentValue:currentValue, Limit:limit}"
```
maria: Thanks — that query helped me confirm the limit is 0 on the new subscription.
infra-bot: Reservation SR#2026-08942 updated: azure-support requested billing owner confirmation. (automated note)
tomas: Also, deciding region fallback: westeurope has spare ND40rs but price is ~12% higher; southeastasia is cheaper but extra network egress to customers in APAC is problematic.
chen: Can we temporarily run training on dedicated smaller NC GPUs (NC24s) in australiaeast while support reassigns reservation? Might reduce throughput but keep latency low.
aj-m: Yes, we can. Need estimate of degraded throughput and cost delta. Tomás, can you run quick perf calc?
tomas: Running a quick back-of-envelope: one ND40rs ~ 4x NC24s for throughput on our model family. So to match capacity we'd need 4x nodes and networking will increase. Cost ends up ~1.1x current reservation if spot rates not used.
maria: Okay — plan: (1) loop finance into SR, (2) request subnet/SNAT increases for new sub, (3) provision temporary NC nodes in australiaeast to keep prod live.
aj-m: I’ll send the support invite and create infra tasks. tagging @maria and @chen for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
azure-support: Update: billing owner confirmed. We’re escalating to reservations team; ETA 48–72h for resolution. If you need immediate capacity we recommend provisioning temporary VMs in the region.
maria: Thanks — I’ll create the tickets for SNAT and VM quota requests and post the links here.
aj-m: Leaving links: https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/SupportRequestsBlade/id/SR2026-08942 
chen: Drafted quota request payload and copied it into the ticket. Also added the subnet port sample details: desired SNAT 8192, NICs per subnet 4096.
tomas: I’ll schedule a smoke run on temporary NC hosts after infra tasks are done.
aj-m: Cool. Closing loop for now — will update thread when SR progresses. :wave:
